headline: Margin expansion drives earnings growth well above sales
summary_short: Grainger reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $5.02B, up 10.3% y/y (13.7% on a daily, organic constant-currency basis), with diluted EPS of $12.01, up 20.5% y/y as operating margin expanded 120bps to 16.1%.
summary_long: Revenue rose 5.9% q/q and 10.3% y/y to $5.02B (13.7% on a daily, organic constant-currency basis), while diluted EPS of $12.01 rose 3.1% q/q and 20.5% y/y — roughly double the revenue growth rate. Gross margin expanded 100bps y/y to 39.5%, including a $43M reduction to cost of goods sold from IEEPA tariff refunds; operating margin rose 120bps to 16.1%. Operating income was $807M (+19.0% y/y) and net income was $570M (+18.3% y/y). The company generated $444M of operating cash flow and $333M of free cash flow, returning $341M to shareholders via dividends and buybacks. Grainger raised full-year 2026 EPS guidance to $45.50-$47.25 from $44.25-$46.25.

drivers.explanation: High-Touch Solutions - N.A. sales (+11.9%) were driven by volume growth and price inflation as tariff costs are passed through; Endless Assortment (+13.5%) grew on strong performance at both MonotaRO and Zoro.
Margin expansion reflected strength in both segments and a benefit from the UK market exit, plus $43M of IEEPA tariff refunds that reduced cost of goods sold.
Margin gain was driven by gross-margin improvement in both segments, sales leverage in Endless Assortment, and the UK exit benefit.
Growth was due primarily to strong operating performance and fewer shares outstanding, partly offset by a higher effective tax rate (24.8% vs 23.2% a year ago).
Grainger raised full-year 2026 guidance across sales, margins, EPS, cash flow, capex and buybacks, citing strong first-half performance and continued demand momentum.
